Bog_of_Allen.json.text: Alend is an Irish goddess. The old capital Almu carried her name. That city ruled the eastern province of Leinster. The hill where it once stood is the Hill of Allen today. It lies in County Kildare. Her name also marks the wide Bog of Allen. People personified the hill as Almu, which means all white. A hidden door to the Otherworld stood on the hill. King Nuada held it first. The hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill seized it from Nuada by force. The hill was named his birthplace. A small mound on top was his seat. Some confuse Almu with Knockaulin.

attributes.attribute: her capital Almu ruled the province of Leinster
her name marks the Bog of Allen
seized the hill from Nuada by force

okr.objective: Describe Alend, the Irish goddess who gave her name to the Bog of Allen.
key_results: Alend was a royal and heroic Irish goddess.

The hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill took the hill by force.

Bolg.json.text: Bolg is a cross reference in this book. The reader should look to Fir Bolg. The Fir Bolg were an Irish race of legend. They were the Nemedians under a new name. They returned to Ireland after years of bondage. The Tuatha De Danann then landed among them. These people were the folk of the goddess Danu. They defeated the Fir Bolg and the rest of the Fomorians. Later the Sons of Moles took the land in turn.

Bolvinnus.json.text: Bolvinnus is a Continental Celtic god. He came from the land of Gaul. Little is known about him. The Romans saw him as the same god as their own warrior god Mars. The sources say no more about Bolvinnus.

attributes.attribute: a god from the province of Gaul
equated by the Romans with Mars

He came from Gaul.
The Romans identified him with Mars.

Book_of_Invasions.json.text: The Book of Invasions is an Irish literary text. Its Irish title is Lebor Gabála Érenn. The title carries the sense of the Takings of Ireland. The work gathers about twelve separate manuscripts. Most are from the twelfth century. Older passages survive in them. The text is poetic. It tells how Ireland was won in six invasions. The tale runs from the great flood to the final settlers. It is a strong aid for scholars of ancient myth.

attributes.attribute: a key source for Celtic mythology

okr.objective: Describe the Book of Invasions, the account of the six invasions of Ireland.
key_results: The Book of Invasions is an Irish literary text.
Its Irish title is Lebor Gal Gabála Érenn.
It gathers twelve separate manuscripts.
It recounts six invasions from the flood onward.

Bors_de_Ganis.json.text: Bors de Ganis is an Arthurian hero. He sat among the knights of the Round Table. He was the cousin of the lord Lancelot. The Grail is a sacred cup. Only three knights were pure enough to reach it. They were Percival, Galahad, and Bors de Ganis. Bors was the least known of the three.

attributes.attribute: one of three who reached the Grail

okr.objective: Describe Bors de Ganis, the least known of the three Grail knights.
key_results: Bors de Ganis was an Arthurian hero.
He was the cousin of Lancelot.
Only three knights reached the Grail.
The three were Percival, Galahad, and Bors de Ganis.

Borvo.json.text: Borvo was the Gaulish god of the healing springs. He is also called Bormanus and Bormo. He is the male form of the goddess Ulkin. The plural form is the Suleviae. Artists drew him as a warrior. A horned serpent rested beneath him. He was the son of the goddess Sirona. He was the consort of Damona, dubbed Bormana. The Romans held he was the same as Apollo. His name may mean to boil. That fits a god of the hot springs.

attributes.attribute: male form of the goddess Sul and the Suleviae
equated with the god Apollo by the Romans

okr.objective: Describe Borvo, the Gaulish god of the healing springs.
key_results: Borvo was god of the healing springs.

His consort was the goddess Damona, also called Bormana.
The Romans equated him with Apollo.

Boudicca.json.text: Boudicca was a heroic queen of Britain. Her people were the Iceni. They lived in the southeast of the island. The Romans broke the priest center on the isle of Anglesey. After the loss of her husband and the ruin of her own family, she rose. She called on the war goddess Andraste at her last hour. The revolt did not hold. Defeated, she ended her own life.

okr.objective: Describe Boudicca, the Iceni queen who rose against Rome.
key_results: Boudicca was queen of the Iceni.
She rose against the Romans after the ruin of Anglesey.
She called on the war goddess Andraste.
She died by her own hand when defeated.

Braciaea.json.text: Braciaea is a god of the continental Celts done in Gaul. The record on him is slight. The people of Rome set him beside their god of war Mars. His name may come from a word for malt. The root lives in Gaulish and Welsh. The root links drink of grain to battle heat. Lords of the Celts gave their soldiers drink before a war.

name may come from a word for malt

Bran.json.text: Bran was a hunting hound in Irish story. He served the hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill. The name Bran means crow. He was born of four feet. His mother was the woman Uirne. She was a sister of Fionn. A jealous rival turned her to a dog. She gave birth to Bran and his twin. Then she came back to human form. The two cubs stayed as dogs. Bran was yellow foot and red eared. He became his master's favorite. He was so quick he could outrun a bird.

attributes.attribute: fast enough to overtake a bird

Branwen.json.text: Branwen is a woman of the Welsh stories. She was the child of Llyr. Her brother was the hero Brân the Blessed. She belongs to the second branch of the Mabinogion. She was given as a bride to a king of Ireland. The king was called Matholwch, and Ireland was his land. Her kinsman Efnisien struck at the Irish by harming their horses. Grief came for Branwen in her time there. She died, and they say she looked like the goddess Rhiannon in her sorrow.
